entities.title: The Inquiry (BBC World Service): Can Gen Z shape a new Nepal?
The Inquiry (BBC World Service): Can Gen Z shape a new Nepal?

properties.caption: Episode of BBC World Service's The Inquiry. The show notes say that within 48 hours at the start of September 2025 Nepal's government was toppled and more than 70 people killed, that the trigger was a ban on 26 social media platforms, and that the protesters approved a new interim prime minister and demanded new elections set for March 2026. The episode asks whether Gen Z can shape a new Nepal, and the notes add that few protests of this kind elsewhere in Asia have produced fundamental social change and that it remains to be seen whether trusting 73-year-old Sushila Karki reflects the protesters' political maturity.

properties.caption: Episode of The Global Story in which co-host Asma Khalid speaks with Anup Kaphle, group editorial director of Kantipur Media Group, about covering the aftermath of the devastating floods in Nepal, the humanitarian efforts, the long-term impact and his concern that international attention will move away.
properties.outlet: BBC World Service, The Global Story
properties.location_method: The segment is not stated in the show notes and the whole episode is linked. Only the show notes were read; the audio itself was not listened to or downloaded.
properties.verified_by: Corroborated on the primary point by: Kantipur Sounds (Fireside); NPR (Up First)

evidence.note: Read from the episode page and show notes; the caption restates only what the notes say. Not linked to the 2025 protests; included because the dataset records the August 2026 floods as the main current crisis.
No segment times in the show notes.
Rule: confirmed only where two independent outlets in the audio set give the same account of the primary point (event:2026-08-bhotekoshi-trishuli-floods).
